newsitem.title: UK: Channel Express says Airbus freighter gets U.S. OK.
newsitem.headline: Channel Express says Airbus freighter gets U.S. OK.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has successfully completed flight tests of the first Channel Express A300B4F, the carrier's sales and marketing manager Tony Carder told Reuters.

He said that Channel Express, a member of Dart Group Plc, expected the FAA to issue an STC (supplemental type certificate) for the former passenger aircraft in its new all-freighter configuration by the end of this month.

"After we get that, we will go through a further certification process with the UK Civil Aviation Authority and we anticipate the aircraft will be ready for commercial service in early July," he said.
Carder added that British Airways World Cargo would not be the first customer of the plane, as previously announced.
BA originally said it hoped to use the Airbus freighter for new London-Tel Aviv flights from January 23.
Because of CAA certification delays, the launch date was postponed to February 20, then to May 1 and then to end-June.
"Because of the (lower demand) summer season, BA has now told us they want to start (twice-weekly) London Stansted-Tel Aviv flights with the A300B4 freighter from September 4," said Carder.
No spokesman for BA World Cargo was immediately available for comment.

"Between July and the end of August, we have lined up commercial work for the aircraft within Europe. But as contractual details have still to be finalised, I can't at present name the customer or the routes involved," he added.
The Channel Express A300B4 underwent configuration into a freighter by British Aerospace Aviation Services at BAe's Filton plant, near Bristol.
The FAA tests checking the aircraft's airworthiness as a freighter took place at the Filton plant and during flights around the surrounding region.
After the first plane, Channel Express also has options with BAe on a further three converted A300B4 freighters.
"We want the first one in service before we start thinking about further options," said Carder.
"A decision on whether to go ahead with any of the options will be taken by the end of the year. It would only take 90 days to convert a passenger A300B4 into a passenger aircraft," he said.
